Hey folks, so i think i found a suitable workaround and more reason as to why this is happening. 

TL;DR, In `Magnet`, if you go to Settings, and disable `Snap windows by dragging` (I personally never use that feature), the issue is non existent. You can even play around with it and re-enable it and notice the 1-2 second lag clicking back into the Godot window.

Using some tools (e.g. `otool`, `nm`, `strings`), I was able to see what Magnet is calling/trying to do.  I provided this information to Claude, and this is what it suggested (Note: I didn't really check out the output to really see if Claude was hallucinating but 🤷🏾 ):

------

```
  How Magnet Intercepts Mouse Events (The Architecture)

  Magnet uses a CGEventTap installed at the system level. From the nm and strings dumps, these are the confirmed APIs:

  ┌──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │               API                │      Framework      │                     Role                     │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ CGEventTapCreate                 │ CoreGraphics        │ Installs a global event tap                  │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ CGEventTapEnable                 │ CoreGraphics        │ Toggles the tap on/off                       │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ CGEventSetType                   │ CoreGraphics        │ Mutates event type in-flight                 │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ CGEventGetLocation               │ CoreGraphics        │ Reads cursor position                        │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ CFMachPortCreateRunLoopSource    │ CoreFoundation      │ Integrates tap into the run loop             │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ AXUIElementCopyElementAtPosition │ ApplicationServices │ Finds the window at the cursor (synchronous) │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue    │ ApplicationServices │ Reads AXFocusedWindow, AXPosition, AXSize    │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ AXUIElementPerformAction         │ ApplicationServices │ Fires AXRaise, AXPress on windows            │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ AXUIElementSetAttributeValue     │ ApplicationServices │ Writes AXPosition, AXSize to move/resize     │
  └──────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Magnet has three event tap class variants — BackgroundEventTap, EventTap, NewEventTap — and a MouseConductor class that owns onMouseDown/onMouseUp handlers, draggedWindow tracking,
   and _isWindowFocused state.

  ---
  The Reconstructed Snapping Workflow (From Debug Strings)

  The strings dump reveals Magnet's internal state machine literally step-by-step:

  "Snapping event taps started."
  "Step 1: No window under cursor found. It's not usual, but it's possible."
  "Step 1: Window under cursor found."
  "Step 2: Focused application is not enabled."   ← KEY BRANCH
  "Step 2: User is dragging window."
  "Step 3: Window frame restored."
  "Step 4: Snapping the window."
  "Snapping event taps stopped."

  This happens on every leftMouseDown, not just drags.

  ---
  The Three Root Cause Candidates

  #1 — Synchronous AX call inside the CGEventTap callback (Most Likely)

  This is the smoking gun. CGEventTap callbacks are synchronous — the entire macOS event delivery pipeline is paused while the callback runs. Magnet calls
  AXUIElementCopyElementAtPosition inside this callback to identify the window under the cursor.

  Godot does not use standard AppKit views. It renders via Metal/Vulkan/OpenGL into a custom NSWindow with its own input handling. Its accessibility server (the process that answers
  AX queries) is either minimal, non-conformant, or slow to respond. When Magnet's tap callback calls AXUIElementCopyElementAtPosition and Godot's process doesn't respond quickly
  enough, macOS will kill/disable the event tap via kCGEventTapDisabledByTimeout (the 5-second system timeout). During that window, no mouse events are delivered anywhere — Godot
  appears frozen.

  Supporting evidence: CGEventTapEnable is imported (Magnet re-enables the tap after timeout), and there's a "Step 2: Focused application is not enabled." branch that suggests Magnet
   explicitly checks if the app under the cursor is accessibility-accessible before proceeding.

  #2 — CGEventSetType mutating or swallowing the click

  Magnet imports CGEventSetType, which lets you change the type of an in-flight event. If Magnet changes the leftMouseDown into a different event type (e.g., to suppress snapping on
  certain windows), Godot may not receive a valid leftMouseDown event, meaning the window never gets the signal to activate/focus. Cmd+Tab bypasses this entirely since it goes
  through a keyboard event path that Magnet's mouse tap never touches.

  #3 — _isWindowFocused state machine getting stuck

  Magnet tracks _isWindowFocused internally and watches NSWindowDidBecomeMainNotification / NSWindowDidResignKeyNotification. If Godot's window doesn't fire these notifications
  correctly (again, because it's not a standard AppKit app), Magnet's state machine might think a "drag" is still in progress, keeping the event tap running in a state that blocks
  click-to-activate delivery.

  ---
  Why Cmd+Tab Works But Clicking Doesn't

  This is the definitive clue:
  - Cmd+Tab is handled by the keyboard event pipeline (Carbon RegisterEventHotKey / the Dock process), which Magnet's mouse CGEventTap never sees.
  - Clicking triggers leftMouseDown, which hits Magnet's tap before Godot receives it.
  - The block happens at Magnet's synchronous AX lookup or event mutation step.

  ---
  Suggested Fixes / Mitigations

  For the Godot team (most impactful):
  1. Improve AX server responsiveness: Implement or improve NSAccessibility protocol on Godot's main window class so AX queries (AXUIElementCopyElementAtPosition) return quickly.
  Even a stub that returns the window frame/PID immediately would prevent the timeout.
  2. Post proper focus notifications: Ensure Godot fires NSWindowDidBecomeMainNotification and NSWindowDidBecomeKeyNotification when its window is activated, so apps like Magnet
  don't get stuck in an incorrect state.
  3. Match standard NSWindow activation: Use makeKeyAndOrderFront: and ensure becomeKeyWindow/becomeMainWindow behave normally.

  For the Magnet team (if they engage):
  1. Don't call synchronous AX APIs inside the CGEventTap callback: Move AXUIElementCopyElementAtPosition off the tap callback thread using an async dispatch. Pass the event through
  immediately and do window identification asynchronously.
  2. Add a timeout/guard on AX calls: If AXUIElementCopyElementAtPosition doesn't return within ~100ms, skip the snap check and pass the event through.
  3. Skip event modification for apps not on an allowlist: If an app's window doesn't respond to AX queries, don't mutate its click events — just forward them.

  For users right now: Disabling Magnet's "snap windows" and "edge drag" features (not just closing the app) may work around the issue, since the "Snapping event taps
  started/stopped" log strings only appear when those features are active.
```

> TL;DR, In Magnet, if you go to Settings, and disable Snap windows by dragging (I personally never use that feature), the issue is non existent. You can even play around with it and re-enable it and notice the 1-2 second lag clicking back into the Godot window. I wouldn't really consider this much of a workaround, as the "drag-to-snap" function is arguably the main feature of Magnet. It's what they have listed first on their website and their App Store page when explaining how to use the program: --- > Using some tools (e.g. otool, nm, strings), I was able to see what Magnet is calling/trying to do. I provided this information to Claude, and this is what it suggested (Note: I didn't really check out the output to really see if Claude was hallucinating but 🤷🏾 ) I wouldn't take Claude's word on this without having people go in and verify it by hand first. What information were you able to gather yourself using the tools you mentioned? That might be helpful for contributors/maintainers to determine what the underlying problem is, and potentially come up with a solution. It's possible that the explanation Claude gave is correct... but it's also very possible it's just realistic-looking AI babble. So having contributors try to use that explanation could end with them wasting a bunch of time in pursuit of something that was never true in the first place. So we'd want to at least verify the AI deductions first.

Fair points @Meorge . I just wanted to share some of my quick findings with everyone for those who **don't** use all of the Magnet features. From what I'd read in this discussion, the options seemed to be either running `Godot` without `Magnet` open, or enabling continuous updates which significantly impacts the CPU, GPU and battery life.

I thought that with this approach, it could be a step in the right direction to getting to the root cause. 

I wanted to share my preliminary findings early rather than wait until I had a chance to dive in fully.
